newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots up.

text.p: Contracts on Shanghai's treasury bill repurchase market closed mostly down on Friday with the end of the issue of domestic A shares by Shandong Lukang Co Ltd, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract plunged to 9.6 percent from 25.01 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover fell to 7.53 million from 11.85 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face-value of treasury bills.
Traders said the issue of Shandong Lukang, the first big firm with a solid results record to list in Shanghai this year, attracted many institutional buyers on Thursday.
"With the issue ended, many institutions returned their money to the repo market today, depressing the rates," one trader said.
Traders expect the repo rates to rebound early next week with more A share issues coming onto the stock markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on Friday after falling earlier in the week, traders said.
The most active three-year note, which matures in September 1999, rose 102.70 yuan from 102.45 yuan. The combined volume of the market rose slightly to 966,500 lots from 856,000 lots.
Traders expect the contracts to continue to rise next week.
